title: New Peso Crisis and Capital Controls Reimposed
reason: Core event is real and correctly dated/placed: after Macri's crushing defeat to Alberto Fernández in the Aug 11, 2019 PASO primary, the peso and Argentine markets crashed, and Macri's government reimposed capital controls (announced Sept 1, 2019, effective Sept 2) — limiting individuals to $10,000/month in dollar purchases and forcing exporters to repatriate FX earnings — reversing the liberalization begun in 2015, with the country sliding toward what would become its 2020 default (a third default after 2001/2014). However, the magnitude detail is materially wrong: multiple contemporaneous, non-overlapping sources (Al Jazeera's Aug 12 2019 report citing Reuters-sourced data, CNN, CNBC) put the peso's single-day (close-to-close) loss at ~15% (peso closed 15.27% weaker at 53.5/USD vs 45.25 the prior session), not 25%. The peso did briefly plunge intraday to a record low of 65/USD (~30% off) before recovering to close ~15% down, and only lost 'about a quarter of its value' cumulatively over the following weeks of capital flight — not in a single day as the description states. Separately, the Merval stock index (not the peso) fell >30%/31% that day, which may be the source of the conflated '25%' figure in some later recaps (e.g., a Sept 2019 Al Jazeera piece). Capital controls also came about 3 weeks after the primary (Sept 1), not literally 'within days,' though this is a minor timing compression compared to the magnitude error. Because the single-day peso-loss figure is a specific, material, and incorrect number while country/year/overall narrative hold, this is a PARTIAL rather than TRUE.
